QF.id: VII Market Participants in Securities Markets_48

question.text: As per SEBI AML guidelines, clients are categorized into risk categories of:

answer.text: Low Risk, Medium Risk, and High Risk based on due diligence and KYC documents
Only two categories: Normal and High Risk
Five categories from Very Low to Very High
Risk categorization is not required under SEBI guidelines

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series VII workbook (page 55), members are advised to categorize clients as Low Risk, Medium Risk, and High Risk based on due diligence and KYC documents. The workbook notes that special categories of clients, such as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and clients from high-risk countries, may, if necessary, be classified with an even higher degree of risk. The Trap: The standard categorization is three tiers (Low/Medium/High). PEPs and high-risk-country clients may require a higher risk classification if necessary, but the workbook does not state they are always classified above High Risk. Note: Source: NISM Series VII workbook, page 55.
